*   **Limitations:** Relies on the accuracy of the segmentation/transient detection model [S1, S2].

The claim states that the evidence relies on the accuracy of the segmentation/transient detection model. Source [S1] explicitly mentions using a Unet model to obtain a 2D visibility map for segmenting transient and static objects, and weighting the loss based on this map. Source [S2] explicitly mentions integrating a semantic segmentation model to generate masks for moving objects (pedestrians, cars) to exclude them from training. Both sources confirm that the methods described rely on these segmentation/detection models to handle transient objects.

*   **Collapse to Zero:** Without regularization, the model may learn to set $V_M$ to 0 for all pixels to minimize the photometric error caused by transient objects, resulting in a black or empty scene reconstruction [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that in unsupervised scenarios, the 2D visibility map tends to decrease visibility (collapse to 0) for transient objects to minimize training loss. It further explains that without the specific regularization loss ($L_{vm}$) introduced to prevent this, the map would mark pixels invisible, effectively resulting in those regions being disregarded (which corresponds to the claim of setting $V_M$ to 0 and resulting in an empty/black reconstruction for those areas).
